title: Proportional Relationships
seo_title: Grade 7 Proportional Relationships Worksheets: Tables, Graphs, Constant of Proportionality and y = kx
standard_text: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship; identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions; represent proportional relationships by equations; explain what a point (x, y) on the graph means, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r).
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 proportional relationships worksheets: decide if a table or graph is proportional, find the constant of proportionality, write equations y = kx, and solve real-world rate problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Proportional means y ÷ x is always the same number, k. Then y = kx.
key_sub: The graph is a straight line through (0, 0), and the point (1, k) shows the unit rate.
body_html:
What is a proportional relationship?

Two amounts are proportional when y ÷ x is always the same number. That number is the constant of proportionality, k. It is the same as the unit rate.

Hours (x)1234
Dollars (y)12243648
y ÷ x12121212

Every ratio is 12, so k = 12 and the equation is y = 12x.

Proportional graphs

The graph is a straight line through the origin (0, 0). The point (1, k) shows the unit rate.

Example

A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours at a steady speed. Write an equation and find the distance in 5 hours.

k = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles per hour.

Equation: d = 50h.

d = 50 × 5 = 250.

Answer: 250 miles

Example

Is y = x + 4 proportional?

When x = 1, y = 5 (ratio 5). When x = 2, y = 6 (ratio 3).

The ratios are different, and the line misses (0, 0).

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Dividing x by y: for 150 miles in 3 hours, k is 50, not 1/50.
  • Using differences: if y goes up by 3 each time but starts at 5, it is not proportional.
  • Thinking every straight line is proportional: it must also go through (0, 0).

faq.q: How do I know if a table is proportional?
faq.a: Divide each y-value by its x-value. If every ratio is the same, the relationship is proportional. If one ratio is different, it is not.

faq.q: What is the constant of proportionality?
faq.a: It is the number k in y = kx. It equals y ÷ x and is the unit rate. For $96 for 8 hours, k = 96 ÷ 8 = 12 dollars per hour.

faq.q: How can I tell from a graph?
faq.a: A proportional graph is a straight line that goes through the origin (0, 0). A straight line that crosses the y-axis somewhere else is not proportional.

faq.q: What does the point (1, k) mean?
faq.a: It shows the value of y when x is 1, which is the unit rate. On the graph of y = 12x, the point (1, 12) means $12 for 1 hour.

items.q: Which relationship is proportional?
c: A $5 entry fee plus $2 per ride
Cost of apples at $2 per pound
A taxi ride: $3 plus $1 per mile
items.e: $2 per pound means cost = 2 × pounds. 0 pounds costs $0 and the ratio is always 2. A starting fee breaks proportionality.

items.q: Which relationship is not proportional?
c: Total legs on some spiders, at 8 legs per spider
A gym: $30 to join plus $20 a month
Miles driven at 50 miles per hour
items.e: With a $30 joining fee, 1 month costs $50 and 2 months cost $70. 50 ÷ 1 ≠ 70 ÷ 2, so it is not proportional.

items.q: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the constant of proportionality in miles per hour?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in miles per hour: 150 ÷ 3 = 50. Not 0.02: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: Ruby earns $96 for 8 hours of work. What is the constant of proportionality in dollars per hour?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in dollars per hour: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Not 112: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: A recipe uses 6 cups of flour for 4 batches. What is the constant of proportionality in cups per batch?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in cups per batch: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5. Not 23: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: A printer prints 84 pages in 4 minutes. What is the constant of proportionality in pages per minute?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in pages per minute: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Not 121: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: 12 pencils cost $3. What is the constant of proportionality in dollars per pencil?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in dollars per pencil: 3 ÷ 12 = 0.25. Not 4: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: A runner goes 5 kilometers in 25 minutes. What is the constant of proportionality in kilometers per minute?
items.e: The constant of proportionality is the unit rate in kilometers per minute: 5 ÷ 25 = 0.2. Not 5: that is the rate the other way around.

items.q: A proportional graph shows hours worked (x) and dollars earned (y). What does the point (1, 8) mean?
c: You earn $8 for 1 hour of work. This is the unit rate.
items.e: The first number is x (hours worked) and the second is y (dollars earned).

items.q: A proportional graph shows pounds of rice (x) and cost in dollars (y). What does the point (0, 0) mean?
items.e: The first number is x (pounds of rice) and the second is y (cost in dollars).

items.q: A proportional graph shows hours (x) and miles (y). What does the point (4, 60) mean?
items.e: The first number is x (hours) and the second is y (miles).

items.q: A proportional graph shows packs (x) and cans of juice (y). What does the point (1, 3) mean?
c: Each pack has 3 cans. This is the unit rate.
items.e: The first number is x (packs) and the second is y (cans of juice).

items.q: A proportional relationship has a constant of 6. Which point is on its graph?
items.e: On the graph, y = 6 × x. When x = 5, y = 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: A proportional relationship has a constant of 2.5. Which point is on its graph?
items.e: On the graph, y = 2.5 × x. When x = 4, y = 2.5 × 4 = 10.

items.q: A proportional relationship has a constant of 8. Which point is on its graph?
items.e: On the graph, y = 8 × x. When x = 3, y = 8 × 3 = 24.

items.q: A proportional relationship has a constant of 0.75. Which point is on its graph?
items.e: On the graph, y = 0.75 × x. When x = 8, y = 0.75 × 8 = 6.

items.q: Sofia earns $72 for 6 hours of babysitting. At this rate, how much will she earn for 10 hours?
items.e: Unit rate: 72 ÷ 6 = $12 per hour. 12 × 10 = $120. Not $76: adding 4 more hours to $72 uses a difference, not a ratio.

items.q: A car uses 4 gallons of gas to go 128 miles. How far can it go on 7 gallons?
items.e: 128 ÷ 4 = 32 miles per gallon. 32 × 7 = 224 miles.

items.q: 5 pounds of bananas cost $3.25. How much do 8 pounds cost?
A machine fills 360 bottles in 8 minutes. How many bottles does it fill in 15 minutes?
items.e: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 bottles per minute. 45 × 15 = 675 bottles.

items.q: A map uses a scale of 2 inches for 15 miles. Two towns are 7 inches apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 miles per inch. 7.5 × 7 = 52.5 miles.

items.q: A recipe uses 3 cups of sugar for 12 muffins. How much sugar is needed for 20 muffins?
items.e: 3 ÷ 12 = 14 cup per muffin. 14 × 20 = 5 cups.

items.q: A worker paints 34 of a wall in 12 hour. How many walls can the worker paint in 1 hour?
items.e: Unit rate = 34 ÷ 12 = 34 × 2 = 1 12 walls per hour.

items.q: A snail moves 13 foot in 14 hour. What is its speed in feet per hour?
items.e: 13 ÷ 14 = 13 × 4 = 43 = 1 13 feet per hour.

items.q: Paul walks 12 mile in each 14 hour. How many miles does he walk per hour?
items.e: 12 ÷ 14 = 12 × 4 = 2 miles per hour.

items.q: y is proportional to x, and y = 42 when x = 6. What is y when x = 11?
items.e: k = 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so y = 7x = 7 × 11 = 77. Not 47: that adds 5 instead of multiplying.

items.q: At a store, 3 notebooks cost $5.40. What is the cost of 1 notebook?
items.e: 5.40 ÷ 3 = $1.80 per notebook.

items.q: A pool fills at 18 gallons per minute. How many minutes does it take to add 450 gallons?
items.e: Gallons = 18 × minutes, so minutes = 450 ÷ 18 = 25.

items.q: A train travels at a constant 80 km per hour. How long does it take to travel 300 km?
items.e: Distance = 80 × time, so time = 300 ÷ 80 = 3.75 hours (3 hours 45 minutes).

items.q: Two quarts of paint cover 150 square feet. How many quarts are needed for 525 square feet?
items.e: 150 ÷ 2 = 75 square feet per quart. 525 ÷ 75 = 7 quarts.

items.q: Lena's heart beats 18 times in 15 seconds. At this rate, how many times does it beat in 1 minute?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds = 4 × 15 seconds. 18 × 4 = 72 beats. Not 63: that adds 45 instead of multiplying.

items.q: A store sells 4 cans for $3. At the same price per can, how many cans can you buy for $15?
items.e: $3 buys 4 cans, and $15 is 5 times $3. 4 × 5 = 20 cans.

items.q: A garden hose fills a 10-gallon bucket in 2.5 minutes. How many gallons does it put out in 6 minutes?
items.e: 10 ÷ 2.5 = 4 gallons per minute. 4 × 6 = 24 gallons.

items.q: An online store charges $2.50 shipping for each book. The shipping cost s is proportional to the number of books b. What is s for 9 books?
Exchange rate: 1 US dollar buys 1.35 Canadian dollars. How many Canadian dollars do you get for 40 US dollars?
items.e: C = 1.35 × U = 1.35 × 40 = 54 Canadian dollars. Not 29.63: that divides 40 by 1.35.

items.q: A scale model car is 124 of the real size. The model is 7.5 inches long. How long is the real car?
items.e: Real length = 24 × 7.5 = 180 inches (15 feet).
